findings.quote: The survivors were not browner or stronger than the beetles that died.
findings.problem: The example's own numbers make this premise false. Before the storm the brown allele frequency was 0.30, and the survivors carry 6 brown copies out of 10 (0.60), so the beetles that died must have carried fewer than 30 percent brown copies. The survivors therefore were browner than the beetles that died, under any dominance (6 copies among 5 diploid beetles forces at least one brown homozygote). The sentence contradicts the very point the example teaches: a random sample of survivors can differ in allele frequency by chance alone. The intended premise is that being brown did not help survival, which the stem already gives with 'at random'. A student comparing the sentence with the numbers meets a contradiction in the key chance-versus-selection example.
findings.source: Checklist B01 (wrong fact); arithmetic from the example's own givens (0.30 before, 6 of 10 after)

findings.quote: In animals, that means the cells that make gametes.
findings.problem: Boundary test fails for animals that reproduce asexually. A hydra bud or a planarian fragment grows from body cells, so a mutation in those body cells reaches the offspring with no gametes involved. Round 1 asked for the limit to sexually reproducing animals; the fix limits it to animals but not to sexual reproduction, although the lesson's own gamete paragraph separates sexual from asexual reproduction. Budding in hydra is standard Grade 7 asexual reproduction content, so a student can meet the exception.
findings.source: Reader rules, Added after the Sol audit (boundary test); B01; round-1 finding on the mutation sentence; OpenStax Biology 2e 43.1 (budding in hydra, fragmentation)

findings.quote: For a question on causes of evolution, ask what changed the frequency.
findings.problem: This paragraph has five sentences, over the one-to-three limit. Still open from round 1 in other paragraphs too: the nonrandom mating paragraph, the gamete paragraph, the second mutation paragraph, the comparing-causes paragraph, the species paragraph, the reproductive isolation paragraph, the sympatric speciation paragraph, the adaptive radiation paragraph and the natural selection exam strategy each have four sentences.
findings.source: Checklist L22a; LSG Formatting rules (paragraphs of one to three short sentences); round-1 L22a finding
